paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's blessing and God's people belong together. David says it's "good and pleasant" when brothers live together in harmony (Psalm 133:1). Then he gives two pictures, oil and dew, and both come down from above. I think that means harmony isn't something we cook up by ourselves, it's a gift that gets poured out on us.

And look where David says the blessing is. "For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore" (Psalm 133:3). He says it nice and quiet, like a man who saved the best part for last. Forevermore is a long time, friend, longer than any batch I've ever baked.

Then the next song calls the servants who serve by night: "Come, bless the LORD" (Psalm 134:1). It tells them to lift up their hands to the sanctuary (Psalm 134:2). And the last line is a blessing spoken over you: "May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion" (Psalm 134:3). So, baker, stay close to God's people, lift your hands to Him, and hear that blessing as a gift from the One who made EVERYTHING.
